LUCENECIO Municipal Local Government Operations Office (MLGOO) DILG-Bobon Field Office Bobon, Northern Samar Dear Ms. Lucenecio: We write in reference to your letter requesting for guidance on the following queries, quoted hereunder in toto: I. Whether or not the SK Chairperson can duly appoint their SK Secretary & Treasurer with the concurrence of only three (SK) Members? 2. Whether or not the SK can disburse and utilize their SK Fund in accordance with their approved SK Annual Budget, through an SK Resolution authorizing the Punong Barangay and Barangay Treasurer to disburse the SK Fund, said resolution having been signed only by three (3) SK Members? 3. If the answer in the latter is in the negative, what will be the process or mode to enable the SK to disburse and utilize their SK Funds? 4. Whether or not the SK Chairperson and SK Treasurer would be allowed to open their separate SK bank account and apply for fidelity bond with only three (3) SK Members as signatories in the SK Resolution for this purpose? Given the interrelated nature of these queries, we provide one discussion. The quorum requirement for SK business transactions and budget approvals is governed by Section 9(b) of the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of RA 10742, as amended by RA 11768. This provision states that a quorum consists of a majority of SK Members, including the SK Chairperson. The default number under Section 423 of the Code is eight (i.e., SK Chairperson and seven members). Hence, five members are required to muster a majority. However, it is this Department's submission that in a barangay where fewer SK members were duly elected and qualified due to lack of candidates, vacancies, disqualifications, or other reasons, the actual number of SK members should be the baseline for determining a majority. Requiring a minimum of five members would render SKs inoperative. "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

Thus, we respectfully submit that a quorum of the SK should be computed based on the number of SK Officials who have been duly elected and qualified. It must be emphasized that the aforequoted Section 9(b) should be read in conjunction with Section 19(b) of the Revised [IRR] of RA 10742, as amended by RA 11768 which provides that "SK Special Elections shall be conducted in case the number of SK officials who were elected and qualified is less than the required quorum." With the phrase "elected and qualified", it is thus evident therefrom that the provision on quorum in the aforequoted Section 9(b) should mean that it does not merely pertain to the numbers, but that the remaining SKs are elected and qualified In fine, our interpretation that a quorum of the SK be based on "those elected and qualified" is impelled by public policy. We hold that the wordings in Section 19(b) of RA 10742 is meant to allow the SK to function even when not all of its entire membership has been elected. Therefore, the required quorum should be based on the number of elected and qualified SK Officials. Based on the foregoing, and in answer to your ISt„ 2nd and 3rd queries, we opine that the SK may conduct business with the concurrence of three SK Members. The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated in your letter and our appreciation of the same, and to address momentarily the ordeal of the SK in your barangay and not in any case substitute the authority of the COMELEC to conduct special elections in your area. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY ATTY. ROMEO P. BENITEZ Undersecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs
